Second-generation bulk RNA-seq deconvolution algorithms

Source: vignettes/deconvolution_description.qmd

Deconvolution algorithms included in the benchmark

Note

Shared notation: Y = \((Y_{gn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times N}\) is the bulk matrix; X = \((X_{gj}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times J}\) is the single-cell or purified reference matrix; P = \((P_{jn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{J \times N}\) is the cell-type proportion matrix. The generic convolution model is \[ \mathbf{Y} \approx \mathbf{X}\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{E}, \qquad \mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{p}_n=1,\quad \mathbf{p}_n \geq 0. \]

See Table 1.

Benchmarking metrics

We compare in Table 2 the headline scores for cellular composition deconvolution, where \(p=(p_1,\dots,p_J)\) and \(\hat p=(\hat p_1,\dots,\hat p_J)\) lie on the unit simplex. Aitchison distance and Jensen–Shannon divergence remain useful compositional geometry scores, but they are not the primary panel: Aitchison is undefined at exact zeros, and JSD is close in spirit to the bounded \(L_2\) / Hellinger family. RMSE and MAE are the usual regression scores; on the simplex, MAE is equivalent to total variation after the factor \(J/2\). Pearson correlation is reported cell-type-wise across samples, not as a \(J\)-vector correlation within one mixture.
